subject: mathematics
question_text: Show that four points with position vectors a, b, c, d are coplanar if and only if [b c d] + [c a d] + [a b d] = [a b c].

verification.note: Source: Sri Chaitanya, FAST TRACK IPE for Jr. Students — Mathematics-IA (2026-27 edition), book p.69, chapter 7 PRODUCT OF VECTORS, Short Answer question 13. Only the question was taken. The solution, the step order and the mark split are this answer book's own work — see docs/ORIGINALITY_MATHS.md. THE MARK SPLIT IS OURS, NOT THE BOOK'S: the Mathematics-IA volume prints no per-step mark allocation on any answer. The split gives half the marks to the multilinear expansion, which is the only real work, and single marks to stating the condition and to the sign bookkeeping that finishes it. The identity was checked numerically on a, b, c, d = (1, 2, 3), (2, 0, 1), (0, 1, 4), (3, 3, 3): the left side [b−a c−a d−a] = −7, and [b c d] + [c a d] + [a b d] − [a b c] = −21 − 6 + 9 + 11 = −7, the same number. It was checked a second time on the tetrahedron a = 0, b = i, c = j, d = k, where both sides give 1 and the four points are correctly reported as NOT coplanar. Paper position: Maths-1A Section B prints eight short answers of which the student writes any six, each worth 4 marks, under the 2026-27 pattern; Product of Vectors supplies one of them. This is a coaching publication, not a TSBIE document, so the split stays unverified until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — the condition you start from, how you expand it, and the two sign rules you use.

steps.label: State the condition
steps.margin_note: First mark. Everything rests on choosing one point as the corner and building three edges from it.
steps.memory_tip: Four points, three edges: subtract the first point's position vector from the other three.
lines: Let A, B, C, D have position vectors
AB = b − a, AC = c − a, AD = d − a
A, B, C, D lie in one plane
⇔ AB, AC and AD are coplanar

recall.must_convey: That the four points are coplanar exactly when [b−a c−a d−a] = 0.
accept: take the three vectors from A and set their box product to zero
four points coplanar means AB AC AD are coplanar
the condition is the box product of b minus a, c minus a, d minus a is zero
A nunchi moodu vectors teeskuni box product zero ani pettali
subtract a from the other three and set the triple product to zero

steps.why: Three vectors drawn from one of the four points are coplanar exactly when the four points lie in one plane, and coplanar vectors have box product zero.
common_mistakes: Writing [a b c d], which has no meaning; a box product takes three vectors.
Using the position vectors themselves instead of the differences.

steps.label: Expand the box product
steps.margin_note: Half the marks. Split one slot at a time and cross out every bracket that repeats a vector.
steps.memory_tip: Eight terms come out, four of them repeat a vector and die. Four are left.
lines: The box product is linear in each slot,
and a bracket with a repeated vector is 0.
= [b  c − a  d − a] − [a  c − a  d − a]
= [b c d] − [b c a] − [b a d] − [a c d]

recall.must_convey: That splitting each slot gives [b c d] − [b c a] − [b a d] − [a c d], the other terms being zero.
accept: expand slot by slot and drop every bracket with a repeated vector
eight terms come out and four of them are zero
what is left is b c d minus b c a minus b a d minus a c d
repeat aina vector unte aa bracket zero avthundi
use linearity in each slot and cancel the repeats
reject: set the box product to zero

steps.why: Each slot can be split one at a time. Every term produced with a vector appearing twice is zero, so only four terms survive out of eight.
common_mistakes: Keeping terms such as [b a a], which are zero.
Losing a minus sign when the second or third slot is split.

steps.label: Rearrange to the required form
steps.margin_note: Last mark. The whole identity is the sign bookkeeping: one cyclic move and two swaps.
steps.memory_tip: Cyclic keeps the sign, a swap flips it. [b c a] is cyclic; [b a d] is a swap.
lines: [b a d] = −[a b d] and [a c d] = −[c a d],
because one swap flips the sign.
[b c d] + [c a d] + [a b d] − [a b c].

lines.text: [b c d] + [c a d] + [a b d] = [a b c]

recall.must_convey: That the cyclic rule and two sign swaps turn the expansion into the required identity.
accept: b c a is cyclic so it equals a b c, and the other two are swaps so they flip sign
after fixing the signs the bracket is b c d plus c a d plus a b d minus a b c
setting that to zero gives the required identity
cyclic aithe sign same, swap aithe sign marutundi
use the cyclic rule once and the swap rule twice
reject: set the box product to zero

steps.why: Cyclic order leaves a box product unchanged, but swapping any two vectors flips its sign. Both rules are needed here, and mixing them up reverses the whole result.
common_mistakes: Treating [b a d] as equal to [a b d].
Stopping at the expansion without naming the two rules used.
